plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic of a single array drawn as a long horizontal strip of equal cells, shaded to mark off four regions. Four italic labels sit above the strip: p over the leftmost cell, i over the fourth cell, j further to the right, and r over the rightmost cell. Three heavy black bars stand between cells as the region boundaries. The four cells from p through i are pale gray; the six cells between the first and second bar are a darker gray; the five cells after the second bar and before the last are white and empty; and the single cell at the right end, under r, is white and holds the italic letter x. Three curly braces beneath the strip label the pale gray stretch as at most x, written with the symbol for less than or equal to followed by x, the dark gray stretch as greater than x, and the white stretch as unrestricted. The shading separates the portion of the array already classified against the pivot from the portion not yet examined. The strip states the invariant holding at the top of each iteration while a subarray is rearranged in place around the pivot value stored at position r.

interactionPlan.concept: PARTITION maintains the loop invariant A[p..i] <= x, A[i+1..j-1] > x, A[j..r-1] unrestricted around the pivot x = A[r]; each iteration either grows the <=x region (swap branch) or only advances j (skip branch), and the final swap seats the pivot between the two classified regions.
elements: horizontal strip of equal square cells representing array A[p..r]
pale-gray shaded cells for region A[p..i] (the <= x region)
darker-gray shaded cells for region A[i+1..j-1] (the > x region)
white empty cells for region A[j..r-1] (the unrestricted region)
rightmost white cell holding the italic pivot letter x at index r
heavy black vertical bar at boundary i (between pale and dark regions)
heavy black vertical bar at boundary j (between dark and white regions)
heavy black vertical bar at boundary r (just left of the pivot cell)
italic index labels p, i, j, r above the strip at their positions
curly brace under the pale region labeled '<= x'
curly brace under the dark region labeled '> x'
curly brace under the white region labeled 'unrestricted'

interactions.label: Implement PARTITION(A, p, r)

api.does: true when A[j] <= x — the only way to test the current element against the pivot
exchange two cells — the ONLY way to mutate the array
attach a short annotation to the current frame for the learner's own commentary

interactions.frame: the whole strip with bars at i, j, r, the three shaded regions (<=x pale, >x dark, unrestricted white), the pivot cell x, the invariant braces, plus the 1-2 indices the last op touched
interactions.sample_code:
PARTITION(A, p, r):
  x = A[r]
  i = p - 1
  for j = p to r - 1:
    if compare(j, x):
      i = i + 1
      swap(i, j)
  swap(i + 1, r)
  return i + 1
interactions.buggy_code:
# Bug: swaps without first advancing i, so the <=x region never grows and the invariant breaks
PARTITION(A, p, r):
  x = A[r]
  i = p - 1
  for j = p to r - 1:
    if compare(j, x):
      swap(i, j)
  swap(i + 1, r)
  return i + 1
interactions.success_check: the returned index q holds the pivot x, every cell in A[p..q-1] is <= x, and every cell in A[q+1..r] is > x
interactions.teaches: Writing the loop and replaying it frame by frame shows exactly how the invariant is preserved: a compare that returns true must advance i AND swap to absorb A[j] into the <=x region, while a false compare leaves i fixed and only j moves — getting either wrong visibly corrupts the shaded regions

interactions.label: Next A[j] case
interactions.teaches: Switching the scenario changes whether the first examined element falls below or above the pivot, so the learner can watch side by side why one branch swaps and advances i while the other only advances j

demo_steps.title: The invariant at a glance
demo_steps.narration: The strip encodes the invariant holding at the top of each iteration: pale cells A[p..i] are all <= x, dark cells A[i+1..j-1] are all > x, white cells A[j..r-1] are not yet examined, and the pivot x sits at r. The three bars mark i, j, r.

demo_steps.title: The swap branch (A[j] <= x)
demo_steps.narration: With an array whose next A[j] is <= x, step the replay: compare returns true, i advances by one and swap(i, j) pulls A[j] into the pale region, so the <=x brace widens and the >x brace shifts right while j then moves on.

demo_steps.title: The skip branch (A[j] > x)
demo_steps.narration: Flip the toggle to load an array whose next A[j] is > x: compare returns false, i stays put, no swap happens, and only j advances — the dark >x region simply grows by one cell, showing why this branch needs no exchange.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The whole of PARTITION is just preserving one invariant: a true compare must advance i and swap to absorb the element into the <=x side, while a false compare only advances j — and the final swap(i+1, r) drops the pivot exactly between the two classified regions.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a single long horizontal row of equal square cells (about 8-16 cells) on a white background. Shade the leftmost run pale gray, the middle run a clearly darker gray, the next run white, and the single rightmost cell white containing an italic 'x'. Place three thick black vertical bars at the i, j, and r boundaries and italic serif labels p, i, j, r centered above their positions. Under the strip draw three horizontal curly braces spanning the pale, dark, and white runs, labeled '<= x', '> x', and 'unrestricted' in serif math style. The code_editor frame must redraw this exact strip every recorded step, moving the i and j bars and re-shading cells to match the current variable values, with the invariant braces tracking the region widths. Wire the 'nextBranchCase' toggle to the editor input: the '<= x' option loads an array whose first examined A[j] is <= the pivot (e.g. 3,7,2,9,5,8,4,5 with x=5) and the '> x' option loads one whose first examined A[j] is > the pivot (e.g. 7,3,2,9,5,8,4,5); flipping the toggle reseeds the input and resets the replay so the contrast between the two branches is one click away.

evaluation.notes: The default static strip is a structurally exact reproduction of the CLRS PARTITION invariant figure (16 cells, correct 4/6/5/1 region split, correct colors, bars, braces, and labels), and the interactivity layer (3-step demo, pseudocode editor with buggy/starter variants, Web Worker interpreter, frame-by-frame playback, branch-case toggle) is exceptionally rich and pedagogically sound; the only weakness is that the strip renders small relative to the source's wide composition.

Refine the drawBrace path to more closely match the typographic underbrace style of the source (thinner stroke, more symmetric curves)
